\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Outer state initialization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, let the outer state be the state initialized using $s$
and $w$, with its source code set to $u$, its target code set to $v$, and its midpoint
set to $M$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial oracle acceptance]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle mapping indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and Boolean strings to
truth values, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,u$ be natural numbers. The oracle
accepts at index $1$ the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary
expansions of $u$ and $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance oracle condition]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle mapping indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and Boolean strings to
truth values, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,v$ be natural numbers. The oracle
accepts at index $2$ the pair encoding of $x$ and the pair encoding of the binary
expansions of $v$ and $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Source register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the source-code register of the outer state with
parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ equals $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Target register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the target-code register of the outer state with
parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ equals $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Outer-search midpoint register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_M}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_M}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the midpoint register of the outer-search state
determined by these values equals $M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial recursion level]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_I}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_I}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the recursion-level register of the outer-search
state determined by these values is $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Outer-search code bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For all natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the code-bound register of the outer-search state
determined by these values equals $2^w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Width register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the width register of the outer state with parameters
$s,w,u,v,M$ equals $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Radius register of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $s,w,u,v,M$, the radius register of the outer state with parameters
$s,w,u,v,M$ equals $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s,w,u,v,M$ be natural numbers such that $s\le w$, $u\le 2^w$, $v\le 2^w$, and $M\le
2^w$. Then every register of the outer state with parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ is at most
$2^{w^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant of the outer state]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $s,w,u,v,M$ be natural numbers with $u<2^w$, $v<2^w$, and $M\le 2^w$. The state
obtained from the outer state with parameters $s,w,u,v,M$ by setting its level register
to $w$ has all scratch, input-length, exponent, power, loop, and popped-endpoint
registers equal to zero; its radius and width registers are $s$ and $w$, its code-bound
register is $2^w$, its source and target registers are less than $2^w$, its midpoint
register is at most $2^w$, its level register is $w$, its endpoint stack is less than
$2^{w(w-w)}$, and its phase stack is less than $2^{w-w}$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.step, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.contH, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpExit, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.cp_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_V, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_inv, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_w, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₂, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E,s,w,u$ be natural numbers, let $b_0$ be a Boolean, let $\text{orc}$ be an oracle
assigning a Boolean answer to each of four deciders and each Boolean word, and let $x$
be a Boolean word. Assume $s\le w$, $u<2^w$, and that for every $M\le 2^w$, the machine
$A(E)$ started at its next-source-search state with register values given by the outer
state $(s,w,u,0,M)$ halts with answer $b_0$, while every configuration before halting
satisfies the program guard with register bound $2^{w^2}$. Then, for every $k,v,M$ such
that $v+k=2^w$ and $M\le 2^w$, the machine started at its outer target-search state with
register values given by $(s,w,u,v,M)$ halts with answer equal to $b_0$ or the assertion
that some $v'$ satisfies $v\le v'<2^w$, the accepting-code oracle accepts $v'$, and
there is a depth-$w$ reachability from $u$ to $v'$ using the relation $R(a,b)$ that
holds exactly when the step oracle accepts the encoded triple $(a,b,s)$. Throughout the
run before halting, every configuration satisfies the same guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Halting behavior of the outer source search]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p005-b004,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b001,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p008-b002
}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.ret, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.exists_shift, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.gb_of, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_K, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_U, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_bd, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_s, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerV_run, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₂, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{7}
Let $s,w$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$. For every $k,u,M$ such that $u+k=2^w$ and
$M\le 2^w$, the machine started at its outer source-search label, with registers
initialized to the outer state having parameters $s,w,u,0,M$, halts with the Boolean
answer that is true exactly when there exist $u',v$ such that $u\le u'<2^w$, the
initial-code oracle accepts $u'$, the accepting-code oracle accepts $v$, and there is a
path of reachability of depth $w$ from $u'$ to $v$ through codes below $2^w$. Throughout
the run before halting, every register is at most $2^{w^2}$ and each configuration
satisfies the machine's precondition.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.halt, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.St.toV_zero, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setup_run, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.size_facts, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a natural number with $1\le E$, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let
$\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four query types and each Boolean
word. Suppose that for every natural number $k\le |x|$, the answer to query type $0$ on
the encoding of $x$ and the binary word for $k$ is true exactly when $k<|x|$. The
register program, started in its scan state with all registers zero and no answer, halts
with the Boolean value of the following proposition: there are $u,v<2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$
such that query type $1$ accepts $u$ as an initial code and query type $2$ accepts $v$
as an accepting code, both at radius $(|x|+2)^E$, and $u$ reaches $v$ in $(|x|+2)^{2E}$
levels under the relation specified by query type $3$ at that radius, with intermediate
codes bounded by $2^{(|x|+2)^{2E}}$. Throughout the run, every register value is at most
$2^{((|x|+2)^{2E})((|x|+2)^{2E})}$.
\end{theorem}
